test_title: SSC CGL 2025 Tier-I Similar Paper (Held On: 12th September 2025 Shift 1)
subject: general
question:
Find the segment containing an error:

(1) What makes the draft law contentious is not the fiscal shift / (2) but that it assumes parity without evidence / (3) among states whose baselines are disparate / (4) and incomparable.
solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

__
 
• The grammatical issue lies in the phrase **“but that it assumes…”** appearing in part (2).
 
• After the structure **“What makes… is not X but Y”**, the two parts must be parallel.
 
• Part (1) uses a noun phrase **“the fiscal shift”**, but part (2) uses a full clause **“that it assumes parity…”**, breaking parallelism.
 
• The correct form should be a noun phrase such as **“the assumption of parity without evidence”** to maintain parallel structure.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *“What makes the draft law contentious is not the fiscal shift but **the assumption of parity without evidence** among states whose baselines are disparate and incomparable.”* 

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

 
• **Option 1:** “What makes the draft law contentious is not the fiscal shift” — grammatically correct.
 
• **Option 3:** “among states whose baselines are disparate” — correct usage; “disparate” is appropriate.
 
• **Option 4:** “and incomparable” — grammatically correct, adding logical contrast.
